note: The Cauchy vectors and Gram limits are in Lean, but positivity is established for word tests (single-point sentences through `Joint.materialize`); the extension of W(F*F) >= 0 to general joint tests by seminorm bound and product-test density is not a declaration.

theorem heated (h : Bid.Hull B Y J) (int : Y.NonTangentialFree W) (v : Fin n → S.Union) :
    ∃! U : Joint n →L[ℂ] V.H, ∀ f : Joint n, Tendsto (hot B v f) (edgeFilter n) (𝓝 (U f)) := by
  haveI := edge_nontrivial n
  choose F hf using fun f : Joint n => vector_limit V.H _ _ (hot_inner h int v v f f)

proof_context.conclusion: `heated` gives Hilbert-space limits of the smeared heat vectors for joint tests, with Gram limits given by the boundary distributions.

snippet.text:
structure Cups (W : Surface S) (J : StarOp S) (K : Spins S) (C : Chamber T timeAxis) where
  hot : Sentence S → ℝ → C.H
  here (v w) : Tendsto (fun p : ℝ×ℝ => inner ℂ (hot v p.1) (hot w p.2)) (till ×ˢ till) (𝓝 (W.kernel J v w))
  omega : Tendsto (hot []) till (𝓝 C.omega)
  time (v b) : hot (K.po (Poincare.translation b) v) =ᶠ[till] (fun s => C.flow.unit.translation b (hot v s))

proof_context.conclusion: `Cups` records vectors `hot v s` whose Gram matrix tends to `W.kernel J v w` as `s → 0+`, from which `Cups.out` extracts the limit vectors.

theorem sees (W : Surface S) (t : F.realizes W) (J : StarOp S) (h : F.sharpPair J) : W.wordsPositive J := by
  rw [Surface.wordsPositive,show W.kernel J = _ from funext fun i => funext fun j => (F.general W t J h i j).symm]
  apply hilbertNonnegative

proof_context.conclusion: `sees` gives positivity `W.wordsPositive J` (an `NNKernel`) of the boundary on word tests from a realizing Hilbert space.
